sprints.name: Backlog R1-R12

categories.title: Use case: codex wiki page tree + labels
Follow-ups from the review of work/quiet-harbor (2026-11-21)

tasks.title: Use case: codex wiki pages + labels on closure-tree (context for R1-R12)
tasks.description:
Context (2026-11-20, from codex / andresbott/codex). codex wants to move its wiki page tree onto closure-tree and add a second closure tree of labels (tag groups, like codex Media's tags). The items in this category list what closure-tree v0.10.0 is missing for that. Each item says what codex does today, what is missing, the required behaviour, and the acceptance tests.

TWO TREES PER WIKI SPACE, both scoped by the closure-tree tenant string "<tenantID>:<spaceID>" (same format as codex media tags: internal/model/media/tags.go tagScope).
1. Pages tree (mandatory). Node table = codex wiki_pages (internal/model/wiki/pagerow.go). Every page is exactly one node; root pages hang off the virtual root 0. The payload is heavy: title, title_key, excerpt, search_text, plain_text (TEXT), doc_id/revision_id, icon, type_key, trash columns.
2. Labels tree (optional). New node table wiki_labels: group nodes at the root ("Topics", "Clients"), labels below them; pages attach to labels many-to-many (zero or more labels per page). Same shape as codex media file_tags + files_tags.

WHAT CODEX DOES TODAY (parent pointer + libs/fracindex; internal/model/wiki/tree.go, trash.go, pages.go):
- Children(parent): one level, live pages only, each with has_children (counting live children only).
- Ancestors(id): walks parent_id one query per level (capped at 1000) for breadcrumbs; trashed ancestors are left out of the list.
- isDescendant: the same walk, for the move cycle check.
- Move(id, parent, after): after=nil means first among siblings; parent and after must be live pages.
- CreatePage: ONE transaction writes the docstore revision, the page row, backlinks, transclusions and refs; the new page is the LAST child of its parent.
- Trash is a soft delete. TrashPage sets deleted_at/deleted_by/trashed_with on the page and on every live page below it; rows keep their parent and position. Invariant: no live page sits below a trashed page. RestorePage clears the flags on the page and every trashed page below it and, when its parent is gone or trashed, moves it to the root keeping its position key. PurgePage/EmptyTrash hard-delete a page and everything below it (trashed or not) in one transaction, together with its docstore, draft, attachment, backlink and ref rows.
- Tree reads never select plain_text/search_text (treeColumns).
- The database is SQLite in WAL mode with one writer connection plus a read pool (gorm DBResolver); PostgreSQL is supported too. A write issued on the base *gorm.DB while a transaction is open on the writer blocks forever, so every tree call made inside a codex transaction must run on that transaction.

EXISTING CODEX WORKAROUNDS (what the items below replace):
- media DeleteTag (internal/model/media/tags.go:392) builds a second Tree on the transaction (closuretree.New(tx, dbFileTag{})) and relies on gorm's nested Transaction turning writeTx into a SAVEPOINT.
- media deleteTagTree (tags.go:433) deletes a whole scope with DeleteRecurse(0, scope).
- several codex tag stores join closure_tree_rel_* by hand for reads (tags.go:594-610).

ITEMS, by priority:
[must] R1 tree bound to a caller transaction - R2 Ancestors - R3 node filter on reads (soft delete) - R4 import an existing adjacency-list table keeping ids
[should] R5 child counts for a set of nodes - R6 column projection on reads - R7 guard against a physical parent_id column - R8 Add placing the node last
[nice] R9 move keeping sort_order - R10 DeleteRecurse over several roots - R11 delete a whole tenant - R12 GetLeaves for models that don't embed Leaf, with filter, order and paging

OUT OF SCOPE: moving a subtree between tenants (codex wiki moves never cross spaces); a configurable node id column name (codex renames wiki_pages.id to node_id in its own migration, see R4); Update with a partial field mask (codex writes payload columns itself and calls Update only for moves/reorders, because Update(item) writes every updatable column, zero values included).

ACCEPTANCE FOR THE WHOLE SET: codex can implement Children, Ancestors, Move, CreatePage, TrashPage, RestorePage, PurgePage and EmptyTrash on closure-tree without hand-written closure-table SQL and without building a Tree per transaction. Every item is tested on SQLite, PostgreSQL and MySQL (make test-full).

tasks.title: [must] R1 Tree bound to a caller's transaction (WithTx)
tasks.description:
PROBLEM. Every write goes through writeTx (lock.go), which runs ct.db.WithContext(ctx).Transaction(...) on the *gorm.DB the Tree was built with; reads use ct.db too (query.go, getoradd.go). A Tree built on the base DB cannot take part in a caller's transaction: on codex's SQLite (one writer connection) a write from inside an open transaction blocks forever, and reads go to the read pool and do not see the transaction's uncommitted rows. The only option today is closuretree.New(tx, model) per transaction (codex internal/model/media/tags.go:413). That re-parses the schema and, on MySQL, re-runs the version query on every call, and it relies on undocumented behaviour (gorm turning the nested Transaction into a SAVEPOINT).

REQUIREMENT.
- A cheap way to get a Tree that runs every read and write on a given *gorm.DB / open transaction, e.g. ct.WithTx(tx) returning a shallow copy with only db replaced: no schema parse, no version query, no DDL.
- Writes on a tx-bound Tree run inside the caller's transaction, nested through a SAVEPOINT (gorm's default), so a closure-tree error rolls back only closure-tree's own work and is returned; the caller decides whether to roll back the outer transaction. When the caller's gorm config sets DisableNestedTransaction, writes run directly in the outer transaction without a savepoint. Document both cases.
- On PostgreSQL/MySQL the per-tenant lock (lockTenant, SELECT ... FOR UPDATE) taken inside the caller's transaction is held until the outer transaction ends. Document it, with the advice not to hold the transaction across slow work.
- Reads on a tx-bound Tree see the transaction's uncommitted rows.
- The original Tree is unchanged and stays safe for concurrent use.
- README section: "Using closure-tree inside your own transaction".

ACCEPTANCE (SQLite, PostgreSQL, MySQL).
- Add + Update (move) + DeleteRecurse inside one outer transaction, then roll the outer transaction back: no node, closure, meta or lock rows remain from it.
- The same with an outer commit: all rows present and consistent (closure rows equal those of the same operations without an outer transaction).
- A closure-tree error inside the outer transaction (e.g. ErrInvalidMove from a cycle): the outer transaction can still commit its other writes.
- Read-your-writes: Add on the tx-bound Tree, then GetNode/Descendants on the same tx-bound Tree return the new node before commit.
- SQLite with db.SetMaxOpenConns(1): the whole sequence completes without deadlock.

tasks.title: [must] R2 Ancestors query (path to the root)
tasks.description:
PROBLEM. There is no ancestor read. The closure table already holds every (ancestor, descendant, depth) pair, so the path to the root is one query, but callers have to write it by hand against closure_tree_rel_<table>. codex needs it for breadcrumbs: wiki tree.go Ancestors walks parent_id with one query per level.

REQUIREMENT.
- Ancestors(ctx, nodeID, tenant, items): loads the ancestors of nodeID into a slice ([]T or []*T, as Descendants accepts), ordered root first (closure depth DESC), with the node itself and the virtual root 0 left out, and ParentId filled as Descendants fills it.
- AncestorIds(ctx, nodeID, tenant) []uint in the same order.
- A root node returns an empty slice and no error. An unknown node, or a node of another tenant, returns ErrNodeNotFound, so the caller can tell it apart from a root.
- An option to include the node itself as the last element (the full breadcrumb) is welcome but not required.
- Honours the R3 filter (non-matching ancestors are left out and the path continues above them; this is codex's behaviour for trashed ancestors) and the R6 projection once those exist.
- One SQL statement plus at most one existence check; no recursive CTE.

ACCEPTANCE (all dialects): chains of depth 1, 2 and 50; a root node; an unknown id; a node of another tenant; the order is stable; after a move (Update) the new path is returned.

tasks.title: [must] R3 Node filter on reads (soft-deleted nodes)
tasks.description:
PROBLEM. codex trashes wiki pages with a soft delete: the node keeps its parent and sort order so a restore puts it back, but every read the UI makes must skip it. All closure-tree reads are raw SQL over nodes.* (query.go descendantsQuery, treeDescendantsQuery, getNodeQuery; getoradd.go findChildInTx), so neither a gorm.DeletedAt field nor a gorm scope applies, and there is no way to add a condition. codex would have to re-implement every read by hand.

REQUIREMENT.
- A per-call condition on node-table columns, accepted by Descendants, DescendantIds, TreeDescendants, TreeDescendantsIds, GetNode, FindChild, Ancestors (R2), child counts (R5), and the node side of GetLeaves. The shape is open: an options struct or variadic options, e.g. a WHERE fragment with bind arguments that closure-tree qualifies with the nodes alias, or structured column = value / IS NULL predicates validated against the parsed schema. Arguments are always bound. A raw fragment is caller code, never user input, as with gorm's Where; document that.
- Semantics:
  - Flat reads (Descendants, DescendantIds): offer both "per node" (a node is returned when it matches) and "prune" (a node is returned only when it AND every node between parent and it match, so a live node under a filtered one is not returned). codex's invariant makes per-node enough; prune is the safe default for soft deletes in a tree. Document which mode is the default.
  - Tree reads (TreeDescendants, TreeDescendantsIds): a node that doesn't match is left out with its whole subtree (the recursive step does not go below it). Its children are never re-parented.
  - GetNode: a non-matching node is ErrNodeNotFound. FindChild: found=false.
  - Ancestors: non-matching ancestors are left out and the walk continues above them.
- Writes are NOT filtered: Add, Update, DeleteRecurse and validateAfterNode see every node. Document that afterNodeID may name a filtered (trashed) sibling and that sort_order placement counts filtered siblings (the gaps are harmless).
- Nice to have: a Tree-level default filter (e.g. "deleted_at IS NULL") with a per-call way to switch it off, which codex's trash views and purge need.

ACCEPTANCE (all dialects, including PostgreSQL NULL/boolean predicates): a tree with a soft-deleted middle node. Descendants in both modes returns the expected sets; TreeDescendants prunes the subtree; GetNode returns ErrNodeNotFound; Ancestors skips the node; FindChild doesn't find it; Add/Update/DeleteRecurse are unaffected; a filter on an unknown column (structured form) errors before querying.

DECISIONS (2026-11-20, Andrés):
- API shape: trailing variadic read options on every read (GetNode, Descendants, DescendantIds, TreeDescendants, TreeDescendantsIds, FindChild, and the new Ancestors/ChildCounts). Non-breaking; existing calls compile unchanged. Writes take no options. The same options mechanism carries R6's column projection.
- Tree-level default filter: a shallow-copy method (same pattern as R1 WithTx) that returns a Tree carrying a default filter, e.g. one "live pages" tree and the plain tree for trash views/purge. A per-call option can still override it.
- Filter form: structured predicates only (column = value, IS NULL, IS NOT NULL, possibly IN), validated against the parsed schema before querying and always bound. No raw SQL fragment for now: the read queries join the closure table, which also has a tenant column, so an unqualified raw fragment would be ambiguous and can't be safely rewritten. Add a raw escape hatch later only if a real need appears.
- Flat reads default to PRUNE (a node is returned only if it and every node between the requested parent and it match), consistent with tree reads. Per-node is an opt-in option for callers that guarantee the invariant (codex can opt in).

tasks.title: [must] R4 Import an existing adjacency-list table, keeping node ids
[should] R5 Child counts / has-children for a set of nodes
tasks.description:
PROBLEM. The wiki sidebar loads one level at a time and shows an expand arrow only on pages that have live children. codex's withChildren (wiki tree.go) answers that with one grouped query per level. closure-tree has IsChildOf for one pair and Descendants(maxDepth 1) for one parent, but nothing for "which of these N nodes have children".

REQUIREMENT.
- ChildCounts(ctx, ids, tenant) returning a map from node id to its number of direct children (closure depth 1), or a HasChildren variant returning the set of ids with at least one. Ids that aren't in the tenant are simply absent.
- Honours the R3 filter: only matching children are counted.
- Set-based: one query, or internal chunks, and safe for thousands of ids without hitting the bind-parameter limits (SQLite 32766, PostgreSQL and MySQL 65535 placeholders), by chunking internally or joining instead of a long IN list.
- Alternative that also satisfies codex: Descendants with maxDepth 1 fills a ChildCount or HasChildren field when the item struct declares one.

ACCEPTANCE (all dialects): a leaf (absent or 0); a parent whose only children are filtered out (0 with the filter); a parent with children (exact count); 5,000 ids in one call; ids of another tenant are absent.

DECISION (2026-11-20, Andrés): a dedicated method only (ChildCounts over a set of ids, honouring the R3 read options). NO field magic (filling a ChildCount/HasChildren field when the struct declares one): it saves no DB work, only one round trip, and it makes the cost depend on the struct instead of the call site. A same-statement "counts" read option for Descendants/TreeDescendants is deferred until profiling shows the extra round trip matters.

tasks.title: [should] R6 Column projection on reads
tasks.description:
PROBLEM. Every read selects nodes.* (query.go getNodeQuery, descendantsQuery, treeDescendantsQuery; getoradd.go). wiki_pages carries large text columns (plain_text TEXT, search_text, excerpt), while the sidebar and breadcrumbs only need node_id, parent, sort_order, title, icon, type_key and updated_at (codex wiki tree.go treeColumns). Loading full rows for every level and every breadcrumb is wasteful.

REQUIREMENT.
- A per-call option listing the node columns to select. node_id, tenant and sort_order are always included; parent_id is always computed.
- Column names are validated against the parsed schema before querying (an unknown column is an error), so there is no injection path.
- Applies to GetNode, Descendants, TreeDescendants, Ancestors (R2) and FindChild.
- Fields that aren't selected stay zero-valued in the result.

ACCEPTANCE (all dialects): selecting a subset fills only those fields plus the Node fields; an unknown column errors without querying; TreeDescendants still links Children; the R3 filter may name columns that aren't selected.

DECISIONS (2026-11-20, Andrés): projection is passed as one of the trailing variadic read options decided in R3 (no signature change). Build R3 and R6 together in one PR, since both rewrite the same read queries.

tasks.title: [should] R7 Reject a node table/model with a physical parent_id column
tasks.description:
PROBLEM. Reads select nodes.* plus parent_rel.ancestor_id AS parent_id (query.go getNodeQuery, descendantsQuery). Node.ParentId maps to column parent_id as a read-only field. When the node table also has a real parent_id column (codex's wiki_pages has one today, and so does any adjacency-list table being adopted, see R4), the result has two parent_id columns. The value that lands in ParentId then depends on scan order, and on which struct field gorm binds when the model declares its own ParentID. At best the physical column becomes a second, stale source of truth. Nothing warns about it.

REQUIREMENT.
- New returns a clear error when the model maps any field other than the embedded Node.ParentId to column parent_id.
- Migrate (or New, with a cheap schema check) returns a clear error when the existing node table has a physical parent_id column.
- Optionally, alias the computed parent internally under a name that can't collide (e.g. ct_parent_id) and map it back to ParentId.
- Document the rule in the README next to the Node docs, and in R4's list of required columns.

ACCEPTANCE (all dialects): a model with an extra ParentID field gets an error from New; a table with a physical parent_id column gets an error from Migrate; existing models and tables are unaffected.

tasks.title: [should] R8 Add can place the new node last
tasks.description:
PROBLEM. Add with afterNodeID nil or &0 places the node FIRST among its siblings, and GetOrAdd always places first. codex creates a new wiki page as the LAST child of its parent (wiki pages.go CreatePage), which is what Update already does for a move without afterNodeID (placeLastInTx, "A5"). Today codex would have to read the last sibling first: an extra query, racy outside closure-tree's tenant lock.

REQUIREMENT.
- A way to Add, and to create through GetOrAdd, at the end of the sibling list, computed inside the locked transaction (reusing placeLastInTx). For example an AddLast method, or an option.
- The existing nil/&0 = first semantics stay unchanged (no breaking change).
- Works with R1 (inside the caller's transaction).

ACCEPTANCE (all dialects): AddLast into an empty parent and into a parent with N children ends last; concurrent AddLast calls under one parent end with distinct sort_orders in commit order; the meta halvings are updated as for placeLastInTx.

tasks.title: [nice] R9 Move to a new parent keeping the node's sort_order
tasks.description:
PROBLEM. codex RestorePage moves a restored page to the root when its old parent is gone or in the trash, and keeps its old position key there. Update with newParentID and no afterNodeID always appends last (placeLastInTx); with afterNodeID it computes a new sort_order. There is no way to keep the current value: moveInTx alone keeps it, but it is internal.

REQUIREMENT.
- An option on Update to move to a new parent without touching sort_order. Ties are broken by node_id, as reads already do. The new parent's meta row is updated if the spacing needs it.
- Low priority: codex may instead accept "a restored page goes last at the root". That is a product call for Andrés, to be made before this item is built.

ACCEPTANCE (all dialects): a move with the keep option leaves sort_order unchanged and the node's place among its new siblings follows it; moves without the option behave as today.

DECISION (2026-11-20, Andrés): WON'T DO. A restored page whose parent is gone or trashed goes LAST at the root. sort_order only has meaning within one sibling group, so keeping it at the root gives an arbitrary position and can tie with a root sibling (zero gap, forcing a renormalize). codex RestorePage calls Update(id, nil, &0, nil, tenant), which already appends last (placeLastInTx); no closure-tree change needed. A restore under a still-live parent needs no tree call at all (trash keeps parent and sort_order). Restoring the old parent later does not move the child back; restoring a child does not restore its trashed ancestors.

tasks.title: [nice] R10 DeleteRecurse over several roots, overlap-tolerant
tasks.description:
PROBLEM. codex EmptyTrash purges every trash root of a space in one transaction, and roots can be nested: a page trashed on its own, then its parent trashed, gives two batch roots, one below the other. DeleteRecurse on the outer root deletes the inner one too, and the following DeleteRecurse on the inner root returns ErrNodeNotFound. So codex must first drop the roots that are descendants of other roots (one IsDescendant per pair).

REQUIREMENT.
- DeleteRecurseMany(ctx, ids, tenant): deletes the union of the subtrees in one locked transaction, set-based, ignoring ids already covered by another id's subtree and duplicate ids.
- Returns the number of nodes deleted. It errors (ErrNodeNotFound) only when none of the ids exist, or it reports the missing ids; the choice is open.
- The same meta cleanup as DeleteRecurse; works with R1.

ACCEPTANCE (all dialects): disjoint roots, nested roots, duplicate ids, one missing id. Counts are right and no orphan closure or meta rows remain.

tasks.title: [nice] R11 Delete a whole tenant (DeleteTenant)
tasks.description:
PROBLEM. When codex deletes a space or a media library it must drop that scope's whole tree, and there is no call for it. codex media uses DeleteRecurse(0, scope) on the virtual root (internal/model/media/tags.go deleteTagTree, :421-451). That works only because of how the virtual-root rows are stored. It returns ErrNodeNotFound on an empty scope, so codex counts nodes first to avoid even creating a lock row. And it leaves the tenant's row in closure_tree_lock_<table> behind.

REQUIREMENT.
- DeleteTenant(ctx, tenant): removes every node, closure, meta and lock row of the tenant in one transaction; works with R1.
- No error on an empty or unknown tenant, and no rows created in that case.
- Documented as the supported way to drop a tenant's tree.

ACCEPTANCE (all dialects): a tenant with a forest leaves all four tables empty for it, with other tenants untouched; an empty tenant returns nil and creates no lock row.

tasks.title: [nice] R12 Subtree subquery builders (SubtreeIDs, ClosurePairs) + slim GetLeaves
tasks.description:
REDESIGNED 2026-11-20 (Andrés; independent review by a Fable subagent reached the same design). Replaces the original "extend GetLeaves with filter, order, paging and count" requirement.

PROBLEM. Callers need "items attached to a node or any node below it" (files under a tag, bookmarks under a domain, wiki pages under a label), plus per-node aggregates (facet counts). GetLeaves only covers the simplest list, and only for models that embed Leaf. codex does not use GetLeaves at all; it hand-writes about ten closure-table queries via ClosureTableName() (media tags.go:604 tagClosure/taggedFileIDs, filelist.go:834-855, facets.go:733, taglevels.go:217; bookmarks facets.go:61-75 and :135, bookmarks.go:1210-1224; projects tags.go:309). They reduce to two shapes: node ids under a set of ancestors, and (ancestor, descendant, depth) pairs for per-ancestor aggregation. Growing GetLeaves into a query builder (filter, order, paging, count over a table the library does not own) would cover none of them.

DESIGN. Two composable subquery builders. They return a *gorm.DB that the caller embeds in its own query; closure-tree executes nothing.

1. SubtreeIDs(tenant, ancestors []uint, opts ...ReadOption) (*gorm.DB, error)
   - Selects one column, descendant_id: the nodes in the subtrees of the given ancestors.
   - Tenant-scoped on the closure side; several ancestors allowed; duplicate and overlapping ancestors are fine (IN semantics).
   - Depth as a RANGE option (e.g. WithDepth(min, max)), default 0..unlimited with the ancestor itself included. This expresses "this node only" (0..0), "strictly below" (1..unlimited), "direct children" (1..1) and "node plus children" (0..1). A single maxDepth int cannot: today GetLeaves uses depth <= max (self included, leaves.go:169) and Descendants uses depth > 0 AND depth <= max (self excluded, query.go:166).
   - Honours the R3 read options (structured filter, prune by default, pruning relative to each requested ancestor).
   - Returns its own error (empty tenant, unknown filter column, empty ancestors) instead of relying on gorm to propagate a subquery's Error.
   - Typical use: leaf.pk IN (SELECT fk FROM m2m WHERE node_fk IN (SubtreeIDs ...)). As a semi-join each leaf appears once with no DISTINCT/GROUP BY, and the total count is the same query without order/limit, so paging and count cannot disagree. Filters on the leaf table (e.g. deleted_at IS NULL), leaf tenant, ordering, limit/offset and count are the caller's plain gorm.

2. ClosurePairs(tenant, opts ...ReadOption) (*gorm.DB, error)
   - Selects ancestor_id, descendant_id, depth, tenant-scoped, with the R3 filter applied to the nodes.
   - Excludes the virtual root 0 as ancestor by default (codex bookmarks facets.go:144 drops it by hand today); an option includes it.
   - Optional ancestor set and depth range, as in SubtreeIDs.
   - Used as a derived table (JOIN (?) AS ct) for per-ancestor aggregates, e.g. COUNT(DISTINCT item) GROUP BY ancestor_id for facet counts. R5 ChildCounts may be built on it internally.

Both are transaction-neutral: gorm renders the subquery into the caller's statement, so it runs on the caller's connection/transaction and needs no R1 WithTx. Build them from a fresh session so no state leaks between calls.

GETLEAVES (kept as a slim convenience, reimplemented on SubtreeIDs).
- Same signature plus trailing read options.
- Accepts any model with a primary key and a many2many to the tree's node type, as []T or []*T (today []*T is rejected, leaves.go:50, and only a direct Leaf embed is detected, leaves.go:62).
- Picks the many2many relation whose target is the node table, not the first many2many declared (leaves.go:88-99); an option names the field when there are several.
- Applies the leaf-side tenant predicate only when the model embeds Leaf.
- Preload of the association becomes opt-in (today it always preloads, leaves.go:176, issuing an IN over every leaf pk, which contradicts the bind-limit comment at leaves.go:107-110 and loads associated nodes without a tenant check).
- No DISTINCT over the whole row (leaves.go:179; costly for wide rows, fails on PostgreSQL json columns): dedup comes from the IN semantics.
- No ordering, paging or count; the doc points to SubtreeIDs for those.
- The depth semantics move to the same range option as SubtreeIDs; document the change from today's maxDepth (self included).

LEAF TYPE. Optional, and marked deprecated in the docs. Decide on removal at 1.0.

PUBLIC CONTRACT. The output column names (descendant_id; ancestor_id, descendant_id, depth) become public API: document them and keep them stable. ClosureTableName() stays public.

CAVEATS TO DOCUMENT AND TEST.
- MySQL error 1093: when an R3 filter joins the node table into the subquery, using it in an UPDATE/DELETE on the node table itself is rejected. Document it (or wrap in a derived table) and add a test. Deletes on other tables (join tables, closure) are unaffected.
- MySQL error 1235: no LIMIT inside an IN subquery; paging always lives in the outer query (it does by design).
- Derived-table joins with ClosurePairs: EXPLAIN-check a facet-style query on MySQL 8.

ACCEPTANCE (all dialects).
- SubtreeIDs: single and multiple ancestors, overlapping ancestors, depth ranges 0..0, 1..1, 1..unlimited, 0..unlimited; R3 filter prunes a filtered node's subtree; another tenant's nodes never appear; empty tenant and unknown filter column return an error before any query.
- An item attached to two nodes of one subtree is returned once; with caller ordering, limit/offset and Count the pages and the total agree.
- ClosurePairs: a GROUP BY ancestor_id count matches per-node expectations; root 0 excluded by default and included with the option.
- Works inside a caller transaction (read-your-writes through the caller's tx).
- GetLeaves: model without Leaf, []*T, two many2many fields (the node-targeting one is picked), Preload opt-in, depth ranges; the existing GetLeaves tests are updated for the depth change.
- MySQL 1093 case documented with a test.

OUT OF SCOPE. Ordering, paging, count or leaf-side filters inside closure-tree; a raw-SQL filter (see R3 decisions).

tasks.title: MySQL deadlocks between tenants: tenant index, automatic retry, documentation
tasks.description:
ANDRÉS SAID (2026-11-23): "ok, capture the details for later implemenation: i want to have the index, the retry for operations where the lubrary starts the transaction and the documentation". Asked whether the recommendations in the notes are his decisions (option 2 of two readings), he answered: "yes, i want 2." and "can you update the task details so that everything is captured and put it in ready". Not started.

PROBLEM. On MySQL, writes of different tenants that delete closure rows can deadlock (error 1213): no index of the closure table starts with the tenant, so a delete of one tenant locks rows of the others. On a Tree not bound with WithTx only that one call is undone. Inside WithTx MySQL rolls back the caller's whole transaction; the error matches ErrSavepointRollback and the caller must roll back and redo it. The only danger for data is a caller that ignores that error and keeps using the transaction.

MEASURED on 2026-11-22 (MySQL 8.0.45; deadlocked calls of 13,500, small table): no index 490; index on (tenant) 34. With refreshed statistics: 395 without, 168 with the index, 0 with the index and a hint on the tenant-wide delete. The index alone is not complete: a tenant holding a third of the rows or more is still scanned in full, just-loaded tables are scanned across tenants, and caller transactions at REPEATABLE READ still collide.

DECIDED BY ANDRÉS on 2026-11-23, by accepting Claude's recommendations:
1. Index: one more index on the closure table that starts with the tenant, on all three databases, through the struct tag. The next Migrate adds it to existing trees.
2. Hint: included. On MySQL the tenant-wide delete of DeleteTenant and BuildFromParents tells MySQL to use the tenant index. This comes back to Andrés only if the MySQL floor (8.0.17) would have to rise.
3. Recognising a deadlock: by the error text "Error 1213", on the MySQL dialect only. No new dependency.

tasks.title: TreeDescendants without a Children field: return an error before querying (review finding 5)
tasks.description:
ANDRÉS SAID. On 2026-11-21: "skip until later". On 2026-11-23, after Claude showed him three options: "I wnat option 2 captured in the todo task in the sprint" and "once captured is is qualified to be marted as ready? if so mark it as ready". Not started.

OPTION 2 AS SHOWN TO HIM: "Return an error before querying. This is the clearest signal, and it matches how a wrongly typed Children field is already rejected. It breaks callers that read one level into such a type, which works correctly today." The two options he passed over: return the flat list of all elements (Claude's recommendation, and what both experts of the review saw as the smaller break); keep the behaviour.

TODAY. TreeDescendants into an element type without a Children field returns only the top-level nodes of the read, without an error: a chain a > b > c gives one element, and deeper nodes are not returned. v0.10.0 behaves the same. A read with maxDepth=1 returns only direct children, so its result is correct today with or without the field.

DECIDED BY ANDRÉS on 2026-11-23: TreeDescendants returns an error before it queries when the element type has no Children field. This holds for every maxDepth, also for the maxDepth=1 reads that are correct today; the option text he chose names that cost.

FOLLOWS FROM THE DECISION (Claude's reading, not confirmed by Andrés):
- A Children field that two embedded structs at the same embedding depth both have counts as none today, because Go does not find an ambiguous field. It gets the error too. At different depths Go takes the shallower field, and nothing changes there. Option 3 as shown to him named this case ("A Children field that is ambiguous between two embedded structs falls into the same trap"), and the expert of the review said the answer to this question also applies to it.
- A Children field behind an embedded pointer to an unexported type cannot be allocated. README and CLAUDE.md say such a read "behaves as without Children", so it gets the error too, also before the query. This case was in none of the option texts, and it changes a result that commit e0a1ddd pinned (readoptions_test.go:688-698). The type alone decides it: the field cannot be reached exactly when a field on its index path, before the last one, is a pointer and unexported. An embedded unexported struct value, not a pointer, stays linkable and must not get the error.

LEFT TO THE IMPLEMENTATION as a small choice (not decided by Andrés): the form of the error. Claude's proposal: a plain error like the one beside it for a wrongly typed Children field (query.go:228), without a new exported name. Callers can then match it only by its text; the other check of this function returns the exported ErrSliceElemNotPointerToStruct. An exported name can still be added later without breaking a caller, which is why the proposal starts without one. The message names the element type and says which case it is: no Children field, two of them, or one that cannot be reached.

WHAT TO BUILD (Claude's breakdown):
- Code: the check in TreeDescendants, where the Children field is looked up (query.go:225-231). It stays before the tenant is validated and before any query, so it wins over ErrEmptyTenant and ErrUnknownColumn. linkTree (scan.go:292, one caller, query.go:259) handles an element type without Children today; simplify it only if the new check makes that case unreachable.
- Tests: TestTreeDescendantsWithoutChildrenReturnsTopLevel (readoptions_test.go:586) pins the old behaviour; rewrite it to expect the error for maxDepth 0 and 1. The hiddenLinksNode case of TestTreeDescendantsChildrenThroughEmbeddedPointer (readoptions_test.go:649, the case at 688-698) expects the error. Add a case for a Children field that two embedded structs share. Each of these three must fail first on the unchanged code. The comments at readoptions_test.go:584-585 and 645-648 describe the old behaviour.
- Documentation: README.md:632; the section "TreeDescendants requirements" of CLAUDE.md; the godoc of TreeDescendants (query.go:184-217), where the sentence at query.go:185, "needs to contain a field Children", becomes true; the comment of linkTree (scan.go:284-291).
- Say what a caller without Children does instead: add the field, or read with Descendants, which takes the same parameters. Read from the code, not run: without the PerNode option, Descendants with maxDepth=1 returns the same nodes in the same order (sort order, then node id). With PerNode the two differ, because Descendants honours it and TreeDescendants ignores it. Confirm the first sentence with a test before the documentation says so; that test passes on the unchanged code.

NOT PART OF THIS TASK (Claude's scoping): TreeDescendantsIds (it returns TreeNode and is not affected); Descendants; writing the release note as a whole (task jrp73mk). This task adds only its own entry, and only if CHANGELOG.md exists already; see the last point of DONE WHEN.

DONE WHEN (Claude's proposal; not reviewed by Andrés):
- make verify passes.
- On the three databases, TreeDescendants into a type without a Children field returns the error before any query runs, for maxDepth 0 and 1. The same holds for a Children field shared by two embedded structs and for one behind an embedded pointer to an unexported type.
- A read into a type with a Children field gives the same result as before: the existing tests pass unchanged.
- README, CLAUDE.md and the godoc state the new behaviour, and no sentence still says that only the top-level nodes come back.
- The break is listed. If CHANGELOG.md exists when this task is built, this task adds the entry under "Breaking changes" of v0.11.0: what changes, and what the caller does instead (add the field, or read with Descendants). If the file does not exist yet, this task writes nothing: the break is listed in task jrp73mk under "ENTRIES THAT DEPEND ON OTHER TASKS", and that task writes the entry. Proposed order (Claude's, not decided by Andrés): this task before jrp73mk.

ALREADY BUILT. The documentation says what the code does today, and TestTreeDescendantsWithoutChildrenReturnsTopLevel pins it (commit b08f4af). A crash with Children behind a nil embedded pointer is fixed (commit e0a1ddd).

tasks.title: Release note for the breaking changes on work/quiet-harbor
tasks.description:
ANDRÉS SAID (2026-11-23). He asked "ok, are there any open questions in the release note tasks ?". Claude showed him six open points: three under "Needs you", each with a recommendation, and three under "Open, but not your decision". He answered: "ok, add as resolution for this task to start a changelog file, use the recomended behaviour". Later that day a check of this text found gaps, and he said: "can you then update the details on the tasks to overcome those gaps". Not started.

THE THREE RECOMMENDATIONS AS SHOWN TO HIM ("Needs you"):
1. "Where the note lives. The repo has no changelog file and no release workflow, and `make tag` writes only "Release version: vX" into the tag. I recommend a `CHANGELOG.md` at the repo root, since the GitHub release text can be copied from it."
2. "Scope. The title says breaking changes only. I recommend the breaks with their upgrade steps first, then one line per new feature of the branch."
3. "Version. The task says "the next tag after v0.10.0" without naming it. I recommend v0.11.0."

ALSO SHOWN TO HIM ("Open, but not your decision"), in short: 4. the list of breaks is not complete, because nobody has audited behaviour against v0.10.0; 5. the entries that depend on tasks w3pwyd7 and dbsbhdw; 6. how much upgrade guidance, with the sentence "You said there are no MySQL production users yet, so a pointer to the README section may be enough." His answer names none of the six points.

DECIDED BY ANDRÉS on 2026-11-23: start a changelog file.

CLAUDE'S READING, NOT CONFIRMED BY ANDRÉS. Claude told him this reading on 2026-11-23 and asked whether "use the recomended behaviour" covers recommendations 2 and 3. He has neither confirmed nor corrected it.
- From the text of recommendation 1: the file is CHANGELOG.md at the repo root, and the release note is its first entry.
- The reading this task is built on: "use the recomended behaviour" accepts all three recommendations. Scope: the breaking changes with their upgrade steps first, then one line per new feature of the branch. Version: v0.11.0.
- The other reading: it accepts only the changelog recommendation, and scope and version are still open.
- A builder does not have to ask first: build on the first reading. Both points are cheap to change afterwards: the version is one heading, and the sections after "Breaking changes" can be removed without touching the breaks. When handing the work back, name scope and version as not confirmed.

Everything below is Claude's proposal or breakdown and was not reviewed by Andrés, except where a line says otherwise.

WHAT TO BUILD:
- First, audit the behaviour changes against v0.10.0 (main is at v0.10.0). The list of breaks below comes from the branch review, not from an audit. Signatures were compared on 2026-11-23 (go doc of main against the branch): exactly nine methods changed (Add, DescendantIds, Descendants, FindChild, GetLeaves, GetNode, GetOrAdd, TreeDescendants, TreeDescendantsIds) and no exported name was removed. Behaviour was not compared. Go through the commits of the branch (git log main..HEAD; on 2026-11-23: 91 commits, 28 of them fix, 23 feat, 1 perf) and place every change a caller of v0.10.0 can notice by the rules under "WHERE EACH CHANGE GOES".
- Write CHANGELOG.md with one entry, v0.11.0, with three sections in this order: "Breaking changes", "New", "Fixed". Leave out a section that stays empty.
- Check every sentence against the code or a test when writing it; do not copy a sentence from this task unchecked.

WHERE EACH CHANGE GOES (the layout had no place for a change that is neither a break nor a feature):
- "Breaking changes": a caller of v0.10.0 has to change code, a database or a server setting, or gets an error or a different result from a call whose v0.10.0 result was correct. Each entry says what changes and what the caller does.
- "New": what a caller can do now and could not do with v0.10.0. See "GRAIN OF NEW".
- "Fixed": a call that returned a wrong result, a wrong error or crashed in v0.10.0 and is right now. One line per fix, saying what was wrong. When a caller could have relied on the old result, the change goes under "Breaking changes" instead.
- No entry: a fix to code that is new on the branch (v0.10.0 never had that bug), and changes to tests, documentation, tooling and internals that a caller cannot notice. A measurable speed-up of an existing call goes under "Fixed" only if the audit can state it with a number from the benchmarks; otherwise no entry.

GRAIN OF "NEW" ("one line per new feature" did not say how coarse):
- One line per capability, not one per exported name. Each line names the exported functions, options and errors that belong to the capability.
- The capabilities are the done tasks of this sprint: R1 Tree bound to a caller's transaction (WithTx), R2 Ancestors, R3 node filter on reads, R4 import of an existing adjacency-list table (BuildFromParents), R5 child counts, R6 column projection, R8 Add can place the new node last, R10 DeleteRecurseMany, R11 DeleteTenant, R12 subtree subquery builders and the slimmer GetLeaves. R7 (New rejects a physical parent_id column) is a break and stands there. R9 was not built.
- Completeness check: compare go doc -all of main and the branch. Every new exported name is named in some line of the entry. A new name that belongs to none of the tasks above joins the nearest capability or gets its own line. On 2026-11-23 the check counted 33 new functions and types; count again when writing.

UPGRADE GUIDANCE (recommendation 2 says "with their upgrade steps"; point 6 as shown to him says a pointer to the README may be enough):
- Each break says in one or two sentences what changes and what the caller does. Steps that fit into those sentences stand in the changelog itself (for example: name the relation with the Relation option).
- Steps that do not fit stay in the README, and the entry names the place. For the MySQL tenant collation that is the paragraph "Tenants" under "Closure Tree methods" (README.md:591 on 2026-11-23). It is a bold label, not a heading, so it has no link anchor: name it, do not link to it. The four ALTER statements are not repeated in the changelog.
- On 2026-11-21 Andrés said about the MySQL tenant change: "exact match in mysql, no migration since we dont have mysql prod users yet". What follows for that entry: the library does not convert a tree that has rows. The entry says that such a tree keeps its collation (with the AutoMigrate caveat the README states), what that means for tenants that differ only in case or accents, and where the README says how to change it.

BREAKING CHANGES KNOWN SO FAR:
- MySQL: New requires 8.0.17 or later. v0.10.0 required 8.0 (dialect.go:55 on main: "MySQL 8.0+ required"), so the break is the rise from 8.0 to 8.0.17. TiDB, which reports itself as 8.0.11, is rejected.
- MySQL: tenants are compared exactly on trees that have no rows when Migrate runs (collation utf8mb4_0900_bin). Migrate returns ErrTenantCollation when the four tenant columns of a tree disagree.
- MySQL: the library's own transactions run at READ COMMITTED. A server with binlog_format=STATEMENT refuses those writes.
- GetOrAdd and FindChild: a Go field name that several columns share returns ErrUnknownMatchField; a list, a gorm expression, a gorm.Valuer or a sql.NamedArg as match value is rejected; a NULL driver.Valuer, a nil byte slice and an empty byte slice of a named type match NULL.
- Nine methods gained a variadic parameter (named above).
- GetLeaves on a model with two relations to the node table returns ErrAmbiguousRelation unless the Relation option names one.
- New rejects a model whose own field maps to the column parent_id (ErrParentIDColumn, closuretree.go:140). New of v0.10.0 has no such check. Found on 2026-11-23; it was missing from this list.

ENTRIES THAT DEPEND ON OTHER TASKS:
- Task w3pwyd7, tenant index: the next Migrate adds an index to existing closure tables.
- Task w3pwyd7, retry: a write on the library's own transaction can run more than once on MySQL, so the caller's gorm hooks run once per attempt.
- Task dbsbhdw: TreeDescendants into an element type without a Children field returns an error.
- Task 1qbqkpj: any of its leftovers that is fixed and that a caller can notice.

ORDER, AND WHO WRITES THESE ENTRIES (the todo list has no dependency field, so the rule is written here and in the three other tasks):
- Proposed order: build this task after w3pwyd7 and dbsbhdw. It then writes their entries from what they built. All four tasks are in state ready, so the list itself does not enforce this order.
- If this task is built before one of them: write no entry for a task that is not built. From the moment CHANGELOG.md exists, each of the other tasks adds its own entry to the v0.11.0 entry as part of its own work, by the rules of this task. Tasks w3pwyd7, dbsbhdw and 1qbqkpj each say so in their text.
- So an entry is never without an owner: before CHANGELOG.md exists this task owns all of them; afterwards the task that makes the change owns its entry.

OTHER SMALL CHOICES:
- Layout of the file: newest version first, one heading per version, under it the three sections named above.
- No entries for v0.10.0 and earlier: the changelog starts with v0.11.0.
- The heading of the entry carries no date until the tag exists.

NOT PART OF THIS TASK (Claude's scoping): creating the tag, pushing, and the text of the GitHub release. Andrés runs the release commands.

DONE WHEN:
- CHANGELOG.md exists at the repo root with an entry for v0.11.0.
- The audit of behaviour changes is done, and what it found is reported.
- Every break listed above, and every one the audit finds, has an entry that says what changes and what the caller does.
- Every fix the audit finds that a caller of v0.10.0 can notice has a line under "Fixed" or an entry under "Breaking changes".
- Every new exported name is named in some line of the entry.
- For each dependent task that is built: its entry is there and matches what the task built. For each that is not built: no entry, and the hand-back names it as still to come.
- The hand-back names scope and version as not confirmed by Andrés, unless he has confirmed them by then.

tasks.title: Small leftovers from the review of work/quiet-harbor
tasks.description:
Noticed during the review and the two fix runs, and not fixed. None blocks shipping. Line numbers are as of the review and may have moved.

DOCS AND TOOLING
- CLAUDE.md:50 says a tree with rows keeps its collation, without the caveat that gorm's AutoMigrate can reset the tenant column.

- MySQL with interpolateParams=true: a *json.RawMessage pointing to a nil slice is stored as '' while the match says IS NULL. Read from the driver, not run.

- New(db, closuretree.Node{}) returns ErrParentIDColumn instead of ErrItemIsNotTreeNode (node.go:27-29).
- scan.go:245,259-265: convertible accepts int to string and narrowing conversions.
- The savepoint rollback after a cancelled write has no deadline (context.WithoutCancel in lock.go). New on the branch.
- TreeDescendants: a type whose pointer-embedded struct holds only Children now gets a non-nil embedded pointer on every element. Side effect of commit e0a1ddd, new on the branch.

- subtree_test.go:805-812: "every pair of the tenant" checks only the duration.
- tx_test.go:365: a 200 ms sleep decides whether B waits on the lock.
